project.title: Determination of carry-over contaminations in recombinant major peanut allergen Ara h 2 produced in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves and analysis of proline hydroxylation patterns
project.projectDescription: The major peanut allergen Ara h 2 undergoes site-specific hydroxylation at three proline residues within repetitive IgE-binding DPYSPOHS sequences. There has been no report of recombinant Ara h 2 production with hydroxyprolines until now. We produced recombinant Ara h 2 in N. benthamiana leaves to determine host-related contaminants and to analyze site-specific hydroxylation of proline residues.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: rAra h 2 was expressed in N. benthamiana, purified and run under reducing condition on an SDS-PAGE, visualized by CBB staining, and excised from the gel.  Gel pieces were cut and washed in ammonium bicarbonate buffer. Disulfide bridges were reduced with dithiothreitol and alkylated with iodoacetamide. Following tryptic digestion, peptides were extracted from the gel by sonication. Peptide samples were separated on an Ultimate 3000 RSLC nano-flow chromatography system with a 30 minutes acetonitrile gradient and analyzed on a Q Exactive HF Orbitrap mass spectrometer running a data-dependent acquisition method: survey scans were acquired in a mass range of 350–1,500 m/z with lock mass on, at a resolution of 60.000 at 200 m/z. The AGC target value was set to 3E6 with a maximal injection time of 60 ms. The eight most intense ions were selected with an isolation width of 1.6 Da with 0.2 m/z isolation offset and fragmented in the HCD cell with a normalized collision energy of 28 %. Spectra were recorded at a target value of 1E5 with a maximal injection time of 250 ms and a resolution of 30000. Peptides with unassigned charge state or a charge of +1 were excluded from fragmentation. The peptide match and exclude isotope features were enabled and selected precursors were dynamically excluded from repeated sampling for 10 s.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data were interpreted with MaxQuant 1.6.0.16 (Cox and Mann, 2008) searching against the databases of N. benthamiana, TMV, contaminants and rAra h 2 sequences with tryptic specificity. Hydroxylation of proline and oxidation of methionine, HexNAc attachments on serine or threonine, and N-terminal protein acetylation were set as variable modifications, and carbamidomethylation of cysteines as fixed modification. The data were filtered at 1% false discovery rate at the level of peptide-spectrum matches and at protein level.  Spectra of hydroxyproline containing peptides were manually inspected.
